title: Neural Network Topology Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for optimizing the topology of neural networks using a combined approach of genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning. The core idea is to automate the design process, moving beyond manually crafted architectures or fixed network structures. The framework employs a genetic algorithm to explore the vast space of possible network topologies, evaluating each topology's performance on a given task. Subsequently, a reinforcement learning agent learns to intelligently adapt and refine the network topology during the training process, aiming to maximize task efficiency. This synergistic approach offers a potential pathway to creating highly optimized neural networks tailored to specific problems, addressing limitations of traditional design methods and potentially unlocking new levels of performance. The framework's key components are described in detail, outlining the algorithms and their interactions. The optimization process is driven by a fitness function that quantifies network performance, and the reinforcement learning agent utilizes a reward system to guide topology adjustments. Future research directions, including scaling the framework and exploring different network architectures, are also discussed.

title: Topological Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum information encryption scheme predicated on the topological properties of quantum states. Traditional cryptographic methods rely on computationally intensive classical algorithms, while this approach leverages the inherent security of topological structures to enhance the security of quantum information transfer and protection. We propose a new algorithm, termed Topological Quantum Information Encryption (TQIE), that utilizes the robustness of topological phases to construct and maintain secure keys and data. The core mechanism centers on establishing a quantum state that is inherently resistant to measurement and manipulation, thereby providing a strong foundation for secure communication. The proposed algorithm offers a promising avenue for safeguarding quantum information in an increasingly complex cryptographic landscape.

title: Dual-Memory Dissociation Under Partial Observability: An Identifiability-Governed Phase Transition
abstract: AbstractWe study whether two latent memory channels, an E-channel driven by fast, high-contrast binary growth-rate switches and a B-channel driven by slow capacity drift, produce a statistically detectable double dissociation in lifecycle model output, and how this detection degrades as oracle feature quality is reduced. Using a controlled simulation framework with three observation worlds, World C, World Hybrid, and World A2, we show four main findings: (1) asymmetric channel damage under oracle-feature degradation, (2) the necessity of per-channel recoverability diagnostics, (3) a recoverability-governed transition zone under true partial observability with decoder robustness across tested models, and (4) an empirical non-recoverability baseline in World Hybrid under tested level-based decoders. All results are validated by a skeptic suite including label shuffle, permuted retrain, feature permutation, column swap, and exact recompute. This record is a preprint version of a manuscript submitted for peer review. This preprint corresponds to a manuscript submitted for peer review. The public Zenodo version is provided for open access, citation, and timestamping purposes.

title: Architecture-Driven Logic Design Strategies for Distributed Educational IoT Environments with Robotic Support
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence components and humanoid robotic platforms into adaptive educational software ecosystems requires clear architectural planning, secure data flows and reliable interfaces between user-facing applications, AI services, databases and robotic interaction modules. This paper proposes a formal architecture-driven framework for adaptive educational IoT environments with robotic support. The proposed architecture is represented as a directed graph, where nodes correspond to software, AI, data, security, and robotic components, while edges represent controlled data flows and communication interfaces. This model introduces metrics for end-to-end latency, communication overhead, reliability, traceability, and risk exposure. A small-scale simulation-based validation is presented for evaluating representative learning scenarios involving AI-based personalization, teacher supervision, secure logging, and humanoid feedback robots such as the QTrobot RD-V2 i7 and NAO. This proposed framework supports students with special education needs by combining predictable interaction, multimodal feedback, emotional literacy support, teacher control, and GDPR-compliant data management.

title: AI-generated, platform-compatible email templates for hospitality marketing: A technical feasibility study of fine-tuning versus few-shot prompting
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is reshaping marketing practice, yet little is known about whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can produce email templates that are directly editable inside campaign builders. This study reports a technical feasibility evaluation of AI-generated email templates compatible with the Stripo template builder, conducted with a hospitality CRM partner. Few-Shot Prompting and Fine-Tuning of an LLM were compared on the generation of Stripo-compatible, non-standard HTML components and of complete templates. Fine-Tuning outperformed Few-Shot Prompting in Stripo compatibility (88%vs. 69%, p = 0.002), generation speed, and cost per output. End-to-end template generation proved feasible but not production-ready, confirming that deployment requires human review of every campaign-critical element. The study serves as an evaluation protocol for platform compatibility of AI-generated email HTML, providing an empirical comparison of adaptation strategies for this niche code-generation task and design implications for CRM vendors and hospitality marketing teams.

title: Superconducting Qubit
abstract: A superconducting qubit is one of the most remarkable inventions in modern physics. This chapter introduces the physics that underpins circuit quantum electrodynamics and continuing on to how the qubits are coupled to microwave resonators. It introduces the quantum framework of raising and lowering operators, which govern transitions between discrete energy states in the transmon. From the Jaynes–Cummings Hamiltonian, the chapter explores critical concepts such as the rotating-wave approximation, and the physical consequences of strong coupling and dispersive (weak) coupling. It reviews the essential concepts from quantum physics to treat the quantum harmonic oscillator. Key quantum phenomena—such as Rabi oscillations, vacuum Rabi splitting, photon blockade, and entanglement between distant qubits via shared resonators—are introduced as the building blocks for quantum computation. The chapter closes by linking theory to practice, describing how microwave components integrate into the experimental setup of a dilution refrigerator to make real quantum processors possible.

title: Rhythms of Work: Multi-Scale Interpretation of Human Behavioral Traces for Workplace Agents
abstract: Runtime traces are becoming a central substrate for understanding agentic systems, yet interpretation has focused largely on what the agent did. Workplace agents face the complementary problem: interpreting the human activity that surrounds them. Hours of low-level events carry rich evidence about a user's state but are too granular to reason over directly, and flattening them into one stream or compressing them into a single embedding both treat "summarize the user's behavior" as if it had one correct answer. We argue instead that behavioral interpretation is resolution-dependent: the same trace should admit multiple addressable interpretations at different temporal resolutions. We construct a multi-resolution vocabulary of semantically normalized operators, recurring motifs, coherent episodes, and day-level rhythms, each preserving the structure salient at its own horizon. Applied to 667 million human-attributed events from a large commercial productivity suite (50,000 users, 100 organizations), it yields 120 operator types, thousands of motifs, 25 episode types, and five day-rhythm archetypes. We validate it on real telemetry: re-running the entire pipeline on a disjoint 2,000-user sample recovers the same taxonomy (structural stability), and on held-out users the full representation forecasts a user's next episode more accurately than a flat-operator baseline, a 17% relative macro-F1 gain (predictive validity), so the abstractions preserve future-relevant information rather than merely describe it. A controlled resolution ablation then shows that no single level is optimal across questions: different agent-facing questions about the same trace are best answered at different resolutions. Behavioral trace interpretation for agents should therefore be multi-resolution and query-conditioned: an agent should access the temporal grain a question needs, not one universal summary.

title: Comparing Retrieval Methods for Academic Advisor Discovery: A Six-Method Study of 768 CS Faculty Profiles Across 9 US Universities
abstract: We present a comparative evaluation of six information retrieval methods for the task of academic advisor discovery: ranking CS faculty members by relevance to a graduate applicant's research interest statement. The methods span sparse lexical matching (Jaccard overlap, TF-IDF, BM25), dense semantic retrieval (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings), hybrid score fusion, and learning-to-rank. Evaluation uses a new domain-specific collection: 768 faculty profiles scraped from 9 US CS departments, with 162 graded relevance judgments (grade 0/1/2) across 5 queries representing distinct graduate student research profiles. Across all five queries, Reranked achieves the highest mean NDCG@10 (0.477, std 0.138), followed by Semantic (0.450), Hybrid (0.421), BM25 (0.406), Jaccard (0.303), and TF-IDF (0.246). After Bonferroni correction across all 15 pairwise comparisons, TF-IDF is significantly worse than BM25, Semantic, Hybrid, and Reranked; no other pairwise difference survives correction at 5 queries. A field ablation reveals that biography alone (NDCG 0.634) outperforms the full model combining biography with research area tags (0.593). A controlled experiment shows that concatenating arXiv paper abstracts reduces NDCG@10 by 0.176, motivating a late-fusion architecture. All code, scrapers, and relevance labels are released openly.

title: Self-Supervised Adaptive Signal Representation Network for Low-SNR Wireless Signal Classification
abstract: A reliable wireless signal classification at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is crucial for enabling cognitive wireless network and intelligent spectrum sensing, however, it is difficult due to deep noise, channel distortion and the lack of labeled data. Most supervised DL approaches require a lot of annotations and have poor generalisation in bad communication conditions. We introduce following an in-phase and quadrature (IQ) concept in contrastive self-supervised signal representation, an adaptive feature refinement model and supervised discriminative signal representation, named as Self-Supervised Adaptive Signal Representation Network (SS-ASRN). It is evaluated in simulation with RadioML2018.01A dataset with various SNR ranges from −20 dB to 20 dB with AWGN and fading channels. The results of simulated analysis indicate that classification accuracy is 96.7%, precision is 95.2%, recall is 94.8%, F1 score is 95.0%, and AUC is 0.987, and the accuracy is stable at low SNR. The proposed framework offers scalable, efficient, and effective solution for smart wireless signal classification in next generation cognitive wireless communication systems by leveraging data efficiently.

title: Indonesian–English Code-Mixed Cyberbullying Detection Dataset (13,677 annotated tweets)
abstract: This dataset contains 13,677 Indonesian–English code-mixed social-media posts, manually annotated for cyberbullying detection by three independent annotators (Cohen's kappa = 0.89). It accompanies the paper "Is Multimodal Feature Fusion Necessary? A Multi-Seed Ablation Study of XLM-RoBERTa for Indonesian–English Code-Mixed Cyberbullying Detection."The data are provided as UTF-8 CSV files, pre-split into training (8,752), validation (2,189), and test (2,736) sets. The classes are balanced: 6,837 cyberbullying and 6,840 non-cyberbullying instances. Each split is available in two variants: a minimal version (cleaned text and label) and a version with code-mixed preprocessing features, including per-word language tags and the anonymized model-input text.Column dictionary:label — 1 = cyberbullying, 0 = non-cyberbullyingtweet_clean — normalized text (lowercased; mentions/URLs removed; slang normalized)tweet_clean_codemixed — cleaned text used for the code-mixing analysislang_per_word — per-token language tags, e.g. [id] kata [en] wordtweet_for_model — model input text, anonymized (usernames -> @USER, links -> HTTPURL)Privacy and Terms of Service: to respect the source platform's Terms of Service and protect user privacy, the dataset contains no raw tweet text and no account identifiers. All user mentions are replaced with @USER and all URLs with HTTPURL. The exact de-identification procedure is documented in the included script sanitize_for_release.py, and SHA-256 checksums are provided in CHECKSUMS.txt.Please cite the accompanying paper when using this dataset.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Machine Learning Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, presents a potentially revolutionary approach to machine learning. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to design a novel adaptive machine learning model, aiming to improve accuracy through dynamic parameter adjustments guided by quantum entanglement. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how entanglement facilitates faster information transfer, ultimately reducing computational complexity and potentially enhancing model performance. The study begins with a comprehensive overview of the challenges and opportunities presented by quantum entanglement in machine learning, followed by a detailed explanation of the proposed model's architecture and the underlying principles of entanglement-based optimization. We conclude by discussing the potential implications and future research directions of this approach.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing algorithm based on neural networks designed to automatically adjust algorithm parameters for optimal performance across diverse tasks. The algorithm leverages a reinforcement learning framework to iteratively refine the parameter landscape, achieving a significant enhancement in efficiency compared to traditional parameter tuning methods. The core mechanism involves training a neural network to predict optimal parameter values based on task-specific data, allowing for continuous parameter optimization. This approach offers a robust and automated solution for algorithm customization, promising increased performance and reduced manual intervention in complex scenarios.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization via Entanglement
abstract: Quantum state synchronization is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing, requiring the simultaneous observation of correlated states across large distances. Current synchronization techniques often struggle with the inherent limitations imposed by the speed of entanglement distribution, hindering the scalability of quantum systems. This research proposes a novel protocol for synchronizing multiple quantum systems utilizing entanglement as the core mechanism, addressing this challenge through a meticulously designed entanglement distribution scheme. The core claim is that this protocol enables the simultaneous observation of correlated states, paving the way for distributed quantum sensing with potentially transformative implications across various quantum technologies. This paper details the design and implementation of the protocol, highlighting its mathematical underpinnings and potential for achieving significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Sparse Signal Reconstruction
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing (QIRC), that draws inspiration from quantum mechanics. Traditional reservoir computing relies on complex, often non-Markovian, dynamics within a recurrent neural network to capture temporal dependencies in data. However, the underlying mechanisms driving these dynamics are often poorly understood and difficult to engineer effectively. QIRC addresses this by explicitly incorporating principles of quantum superposition and entanglement into the reservoir design. The core idea is to construct a reservoir with dynamics mimicking the behavior of a quantum system, allowing for exponentially increased state space representation without the need for computationally expensive quantum hardware. This paper details the theoretical framework, the design considerations for a QIRC system, and presents a simple linear readout layer to reconstruct sparse signals from noisy input. We demonstrate that by leveraging quantum-inspired dynamics, QIRC offers a potential pathway to improved performance in scenarios involving sparse signal reconstruction, particularly where the underlying signal structure is complex and difficult to model using conventional reservoir computing methods. The key mathematical formulations and operational definitions are presented, highlighting the core concepts and providing a foundation for future research and development.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding and decoding, termed Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE), leveraging the unique properties of multi-body quantum entanglement. The core claim is that utilizing multi-particle entanglement enables a fundamentally new information encoding and decoding paradigm, surpassing the limitations imposed by classical information theory and achieving unprecedented density and speed of information transfer. The proposed mechanism involves designing a system capable of dynamically generating and controlling multi-body entangled states. Information is encoded within the entangled states, and decoding is performed utilizing the inherent correlations within these states. The novelty of QIE lies in its exploitation of multi-body entanglement, which offers potential advantages in both encoding density and transmission speed compared to existing single-particle entanglement-based methods. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the key principles and considerations for developing and implementing a QIE system, focusing on the control and manipulation of complex entangled states for efficient information processing.

title: Contextualized Symbolic Regression with Hierarchical Grammars
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) offers a powerful approach to discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance is often limited by its sensitivity to noise, the need for extensive manual feature engineering, and difficulty in handling complex, high-dimensional datasets. This paper introduces a novel system combining symbolic regression with hierarchical grammars and contextualized feature learning. The system constructs a hierarchical grammar that represents the underlying mathematical relationships, while simultaneously learning contextualized features to refine the model's accuracy and robustness. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional SR by enabling automatic discovery of complex models from noisy data. The core claim is that the proposed system significantly improves the flexibility and robustness of SR. The system learns a grammar that can adapt to the data's inherent structure, improving accuracy and reducing the dependency on manual intervention. The system's key innovation lies in the integration of hierarchical grammar learning with contextualized feature extraction. This allows the system to effectively handle complex relationships and improve the overall effectiveness of the symbolic regression process. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining its architecture and expected behavior.

title: Information-Theoretic Constraint-Based Adversarial Training
abstract: Adversarial training, a cornerstone of robust machine learning, frequently struggles with instability and vulnerability to minor perturbations. This work introduces a novel approach to adversarial training that leverages information-theoretic constraints, specifically mutual information, to address these shortcomings. The core idea is to penalize the generator for reducing the mutual information between its output and the discriminator's features. This constraint forces the generator to create adversarial examples that are genuinely disruptive and less susceptible to small, targeted attacks. We demonstrate that incorporating this information-theoretic perspective leads to more stable training, generates more effective adversarial examples, and ultimately, improves the robustness of the defended model. The method offers a quantifiable measure of disruption, moving beyond simple loss function optimization and providing a stronger theoretical foundation for adversarial training.

title: Nonlinear Topological Topology Structures in Quantum Algorithm Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of nonlinear topological topology structures within quantum algorithm computation, aiming to enhance efficiency and stability. We explore a novel quantum algorithm design framework predicated on these structures, presenting a potential pathway towards improved quantum computation. The core claim is that leveraging these topological properties can significantly accelerate and stabilize quantum computations. This work introduces a framework that utilizes the inherent properties of topological structures to optimize quantum algorithm design.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics via Non-Local Constraint Propagation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds profound implications for technology and fundamental physics. However, accurately modeling and controlling entangled states, particularly over long distances, remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Quantum Entanglement Dynamics via Non-Local Constraint Propagation, which utilizes a dynamically evolving Constraint Field to quantify and manipulate entanglement dynamics. We move beyond traditional quantum mechanics by introducing a fundamentally adjustable geometric structure that allows for precise control and deeper understanding of entanglement correlations. This approach offers the potential for unprecedented manipulation of entangled states, opening avenues for advanced quantum communication and computation.

This approach offers the potential for unprecedented manipulation of entangled states, opening avenues for advanced quantum communication and computation.

title: Formal Model of Cognitive Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper presents a formal mathematical model to analyze the propagation of cognitive biases within multi-agent systems. The core claim is that biases, initially present in individual agents, can systematically spread through interactions, generating systemic errors. The model incorporates key factors such as agent communication, influence dynamics, and feedback loops, all represented through mathematical equations. We define a set of variables representing agent beliefs, biases, and interaction parameters. The model then utilizes differential equations to describe the evolution of these variables over time, capturing the dynamic process of bias propagation. Specifically, we introduce a bias transmission rate (β), an influence factor (γ), and a feedback sensitivity (δ) to quantify the mechanisms driving the spread. The model is designed to provide a framework for quantifying the impact of cognitive biases and for developing strategies to mitigate their propagation. The model's outputs provide a quantifiable measure of bias amplification and allow for the evaluation of different intervention strategies. Further, the model's simplicity allows for a range of simulations to test various scenarios.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state optimization algorithm based on an adaptive Turing machine. Traditional quantum state optimization methods often employ static parameter adjustments, limiting their ability to adapt to complex quantum systems. This paper proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism utilizing an adaptive Turing machine, enabling the algorithm to dynamically adjust quantum state parameters to achieve higher precision and adaptability. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations. The core mechanism involves defining a set of adaptive rules based on quantum state characteristics, allowing the algorithm to iteratively refine the state to minimize an objective function. This results in improved performance across a range of quantum measurement tasks.

title: Dynamic Graph Structure Parameter Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic graph structure parameter learning algorithm designed to automate parameter optimization. Traditional parameter adjustment methods rely on manual tuning, while this algorithm leverages graph structure to model the system, dynamically adjusting graph properties to optimize performance. We propose a framework that iteratively refines the graph structure based on feedback from the system, enabling efficient and adaptive parameter learning. The core mechanism centers around a graph transformation process that iteratively adjusts node and edge weights, resulting in a more informative and adaptable representation of the system. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of simulations, showcasing the ability to achieve superior performance compared to traditional optimization techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement State Modeling: A Novel Approach to Non-Linear Geometric Distribution
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing information storage and transmission. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to the development of a novel non-linear geometric distribution model for describing quantum information. We propose a framework centered around the concept of entangled states as the fundamental building blocks of quantum information, aiming to capture and manipulate the intricate interplay of quantum states. This model incorporates a unique geometric distribution approach, enabling precise modeling of quantum state evolution and facilitating enhanced quantum information encoding and transmission capabilities. The core claim is that this model offers a significantly enhanced approach to quantum information handling compared to existing approaches. We detail the model's architecture, mathematical foundation, and potential applications, highlighting the novel mechanisms and the benefits derived from incorporating entanglement into the geometric distribution framework. The work introduces a new perspective on quantum information management, focusing on the interplay between entangled states and geometric distributions.

title: Title: Adaptive Learning for Complex System Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning algorithm for complex system optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the algorithm's adaptability to different input data. This paper proposes a new approach that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the input data, resulting in more efficient and robust optimization. The core mechanism involves utilizing an adaptive learning algorithm to fine-tune parameters during the optimization process, addressing the limitations of static optimization techniques. This work demonstrates improved performance on a suite of complex system optimization tasks, highlighting the advantages of dynamic parameter adjustment.

title: Title: Hermetic Quantum Complexity (HQC)
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit an unprecedented level of complexity, often exceeding classical systems in terms of interdependencies and emergent properties. Traditional approaches to understanding and controlling this complexity struggle to effectively predict and manage it. This paper proposes a novel framework, Hermetic Quantum Complexity (HQC), which leverages the principles of hermetic states – highly ordered quantum states – to quantify and manage this complexity. We develop a method for mapping quantum states to a complexity metric, enabling precise prediction and control of complex behavior. The core mechanism of HQC involves a sophisticated mapping algorithm that analyzes quantum states to identify the underlying structure and generate a complexity score. This score can then be used to guide the design of quantum systems with desired characteristics. This approach offers a robust and quantitative methodology for tackling the challenges posed by quantum complexity, potentially leading to significant advancements in quantum algorithm design, simulation, and control. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future directions of this research.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Synchronization Protocols
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionary technologies, including quantum computing and quantum communication. However, maintaining the stability of entangled states over long distances presents a significant hurdle. This paper investigates a novel protocol for precisely synchronizing quantum entanglement across multiple qubits, utilizing delayed-quantum measurements and error correction within a dynamically-changing entangled state. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically-adjusted synchronization matrix designed to minimize error rates and enhance entanglement fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through rigorous simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the stability and utilization of quantum entanglement.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Entropy Adaptive Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential for revolutionary computational capabilities. This paper explores the application of entanglement-based information entropy to a novel adaptive computing approach. We propose a method that leverages the unique properties of entangled quantum states to achieve precise computations and information extraction across a broader range of quantum systems. This work investigates the design of a specialized calculation model based on entangled states, emphasizing the extraction and analysis of entangled states. The core claim is that this approach offers significantly enhanced computational efficiency and precision compared to traditional methods, particularly for complex quantum states. The research will demonstrate the feasibility of scaling this approach to more complex sub-systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Calculations: Adaptive Correction
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents significant challenges for computation due to its inherent fragility and sensitivity to environmental disturbances. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on meticulously calibrated parameters, limiting their adaptability and efficiency. This paper introduces an innovative adaptive correction mechanism for quantum entanglement calculations, leveraging the dynamic nature of entangled states to automatically adjust parameters and dramatically improve the precision and efficiency of these calculations. The core mechanism involves employing a self-corrective algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters based on real-time entanglement fluctuations, effectively mitigating the effects of these fluctuations and achieving a higher fidelity outcome. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in current quantum computing techniques, paving the way for more robust and versatile algorithms.

title: Quantum Resonance-Based Algorithm for Prime Number Distribution
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm, the Quantum Resonance-Based Algorithm (QRBA), designed to efficiently distribute prime numbers within a defined range. Leveraging the principles of quantum resonance, we propose a mechanism that amplifies the probability of prime number generation, offering a potentially exponential speed-up compared to classical methods. The core of this algorithm centers on the manipulation of quantum superposition and entanglement to generate a 'resonance field' that enhances the likelihood of prime number occurrence. The theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrate the algorithm's potential for significant performance improvements in prime number distribution.

title: Dynamic Topology Optimization of Quantum States
abstract: Quantum state optimization is a challenging and critical task in quantum computing and quantum information science. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively adapt to the complex, non-linear nature of quantum systems, leading to suboptimal solutions. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology optimization algorithm, designed to automatically adjust quantum state topology, thereby optimizing quantum system performance. The core mechanism leverages the inherent topological structure of quantum states, coupled with quantum error correction, to achieve adaptive and robust optimization. This approach overcomes limitations of static optimization techniques and offers a promising path toward efficient quantum state engineering.

title: The Inversion of Trust: Vocabulary-Bounded Security in Protocol-Governed Systems
abstract: This paper analyzes the security properties that emerge structurally from protocol-governed architecture. Building on the deterministic enforcement model (Paper 6) [Bachi, 2026f] and the computation-mutation separation (Paper 7) [Bachi, 2026g], we demonstrate that protocol governance inverts conventional trust assumptions. Rather than trusting implementation code, protocol-governed systems trust ratified behavioral law. Rather than defending against implicit behavior, they eliminate undeclared behavior. Rather than constraining execution with runtime guards, they bound mutation through vocabulary and constitutional enforcement.

title: AI Fluency Feedback Experiment (September 2026)
abstract: This is our first study of our initiative's (https://ai-ready-workforce.ai.cornell.edu/) AI fluency assessment platform. The goal is to collect data on how people approach a complex task using AI to help them, and to test if the feedback we AI-generate using the behavioral trace data is effective at improving performance on a subsequent, isomorphic task. We recruit a US census-aligned sample of 200 participants, everyone completes the same two isomorphic activities, in-between they are randomized to either get feedback on their process or they get a self-reflection prompt. We examine changes in the scores between the two tasks. We also examine if AI literacy survey measures correlate with the behavioral evidence we collect.

title: Enhancing Solar Power Forecasting Accuracy Using HMPCS and Machine Learning Techniques: An Applied Study
abstract: Background Solar irradiance is a nonlinear and intermittent function, which makes accurate forecasting of solar power generation a challenge. The high variability of meteorological conditions is not well represented by conventional atmospheric models, thus hampering forecasting skill and model robustness. In this work, an advanced hybridization of multi-population cuckoo search (HMPCS) algorithm with machine learning (ML) methods is developed to enhance the predicated performance of photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting with more reliability. Methods In this study, a hybrid modeling framework is proposed, called HMPCS–ML framework which captures the global search capacity of HMPCS and predictive power of sophisticated ML models (Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)). Optimizing hyperparameters by balancing exploration and exploitation, the algorithm runs on multi-populations through Lévy flight randomization. Interpolation, normalization, and temporal windowing were utilized to preprocess synthetic meteorological and irradiance datasets. We evaluated the framework by comparing commonly used statistical measures (MAE, RMSE, MAPE, R 2 ). Results Moreover, experimental analyses showed that HMPCS–ML models significantly outperformed baseline approaches (Grid Search and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)). Results showed that the optimized LSTM+HMPCS model outperformed other models in terms of lowest RMSE (0.139) and highest R 2 (0.93), reflecting the LSTM model’s good fit with practical observations and generalization ability. The optimal LightGBM+HMPCS variant also proved to be consistently better, with reduced error (23% lower than unoptimized models). Conclusions In this regard, the HMPCS–ML framework is a powerful and efficient solution for the optimization of Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, improving the predictive performance and calculation efficiency. This research shows the potential of hybrid metaheuristic–ML integration for renewable energy prediction and smart-grid applications in general and indicates further extensions to multi-objective and Transformer-based architectures.

title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
abstract: Language-model judges now gate training data, score generations, and drive leaderboards. The judge is then a measurement instrument, resting on one rarely stated assumption: the same request, sent to the same model name, reads the same tomorrow. We audited that assumption in two preregistered campaigns with every threshold fixed in advance; neither got past validating its instrument. Across 52,988 audited request attempts, same-window repeat rankings agreed at Spearman 0.400 against a required 0.90, and byte-identical next-day replays agreed at 0.78 against a required 0.99, each time with the execution record at ceiling. Three mechanisms explain the gap: a label-to-meaning mapping that biased readouts as strongly as the signal; candidate gaps seven orders of magnitude below the instrument's own noise floor; and byte-identical inputs returning different rankings, a noise that exact-permutation readouts compound. Neither metric substitution nor sampling repaired it on the tested grid. Preregistered follow-ups bound the problem: waiting did not help on the days sampled (0.805 versus 0.800, replicated over five further days); switching providers did not help (four providers share the floor, medians 0.74 to 0.88, predicted by none of the metadata fields they expose); self-hosting on batch-invariant kernels helped only while the server was quiet; and on constructed errors with known gaps, the readout's separation tracks error type, not size. We distill the evidence into a three-level snapshot-identity ladder, eight design rules, and a reporting checklist; a pilot at roughly 2% of the study's call volume would have exposed both unreachable gates in advance. All results concern externally measured behaviour on shared serving infrastructure. On a shared endpoint, a model name is not a frozen instrument; a preregistered evaluation must measure its instrument before freezing any gate on it.

title: Residual neural networks overcome the curse of dimensionality for semilinear heat equations
abstract: Rigorous results show that feedforward neural networks can overcome the curse of dimensionality in the numerical approximation of high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs), but comparatively little is known about residual neural networks (ResNets) in the nonlinear PDE setting. We prove that ResNets overcome the curse of dimensionality in the numerical approximation of solutions of semilinear heat equations with globally Lipschitz continuous, gradient-independent nonlinearities: under polynomial growth and network approximability hypotheses on the PDE data, there exist $η\in(0,\infty)$ and ResNets $Ψ_{d,\varepsilon}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, with at most $ηd^η\varepsilon^{-η}$ parameters whose realizations approximate the solution in dimension $d$ with an $L^2$-error of at most $\varepsilon$. The proof represents one deterministic realization of a multilevel Picard estimator by a ResNet whose shortcut connections transmit the spatial variable and a scalar accumulator, while the residual branches successively add the summands of the estimator. For ridge-sum initial conditions, admissible sigmoidal activations, and globally Lipschitz truncations of the nonlinearity, we obtain, for every $ξ>0$, the explicit bound $C_ξd^{4+ξ}\varepsilon^{-(3+ξ)}$ on the number of parameters.

title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus
abstract: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. Here we propose that their diffusion can be understood through a viral analogy, with LLM use spreading through populations, becoming embedded in cognitive and cultural practices. We model transitions among uncoupled, coupled, and persistently dependent users, and show that the interplay between social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement can generate tipping points and technological lock-in. A central consequence is the possibility of runaway dynamics: once a critical threshold is crossed, small increases in adoption can trigger rapid population-level shifts toward persistent dependence, with abrupt losses in cognitive competence. The same framework, however, identifies conditions for cognitive immunization, based on reducing transmission and facilitating reversibility. Our results highlight how LLM adoption may involve nonlinear collective transitions with important consequences for cognitive autonomy.

abstract: يسعى هذا البحث إلى تقديم رؤية لسانية حاسوبية معاصرة للبنية الصرفية في "رسالة الحقوق" للإمام زين العابدين (عليه السلام)، عبر أتمتة التحليل الصرفي لأبنية الأفعال وتوصيفها صورياً. ونظراً لكون النص يمثل وثيقة تشريعية وأخلاقية رفيعة، فقد اعتمد البحث "خط معالجة آلي" (Pipeline) يزاوج بين القواعد الصرفية التراثية وخوارزميات معالجة اللغات الطبيعية(NLP)، وتأسيساً على مخرجات المحلل الصرفي المقترح، كشفت الدراسة عن "بصمة صرفية" مائزة تمثلت في هيمنة الفعل الثلاثي المجرد لتقرير الحقوق، وتنامي الأوزان المزيدة (أَفْعَلَ، تَفَعَّلَ، اسْتَفْعَلَ) في سياقات الإلزام والطلب والمشاركة. ومن ناحية أخرى، أثبتت النتائج الإحصائية كفاءة الأتمتة في معالجة الغموض الصرفي وتحليل المورفيمات الصفرية بدقة بلغت 92%، مما يؤكد قابلية النصوص التراثية للرقمنة مع الحفاظ على عمقها الدلالي والروحي.

title: Quantum Information Entropy Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces a novel protocol, the Quantum Information Entropy Protocol, designed to quantify and understand the information entropy of quantum systems. Traditional entropy calculations rely on classical computation, which becomes inadequate for complex quantum systems. This protocol leverages the inherent statistical properties of quantum information, utilizing the calculation of quantum information entropy to provide a more precise and insightful model for quantum system evolution and properties. The core mechanism involves establishing a protocol based on quantum error correction and quantum key distribution, where the calculation of quantum information entropy serves as the foundation for understanding the system's dynamics. This approach offers a fundamentally different methodology for analyzing and characterizing quantum systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm designed for high-dimensional geometric data distributions. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with data distribution changes, necessitating dynamic modeling approaches. Our algorithm employs an adaptive clustering process, dynamically adjusting cluster parameters based on the data distribution's evolution. This adaptation ensures higher precision in data clustering and feature extraction, ultimately optimizing the resulting data structure. We explore the potential of this approach to address challenges in analyzing and understanding complex geometric datasets.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometry Transformation Generation based on Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize geometry generation, addressing the computational challenges inherent in creating complex geometric transformations. We propose a novel paradigm leveraging quantum computation to design and optimize geometric transformations, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical methods. The core mechanism centers around quantum algorithms for generating and refining geometric primitives, offering a fundamentally different approach to complex shape creation. This research investigates the feasibility of quantum computing for handling geometric transformations with increased efficiency and precision, ultimately leading to a new generation of computational tools for geometric modeling and design. Specifically, we detail the design of a quantum algorithm for generating and manipulating geometric transformations, emphasizing its potential to overcome the computational bottlenecks encountered in traditional approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum Entanglement Mapping Algorithm: A Novel Approach to Non-Locality and Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to information processing and computation. The inherent non-locality of entangled particles – the ability to instantaneously influence distant states – has long been considered a bottleneck for developing practical quantum technologies. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Quantum Entanglement Mapping Algorithm (QEMA), designed to overcome these limitations by leveraging entanglement to achieve information transfer and manipulation beyond the limitations imposed by local realism. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of a "纠缠矩阵" – a mathematical representation of the entangled state – which allows for the implementation of a "multi-universe" model, enhancing computational capabilities.

title: Multi-Agent Systems with Emergent Social Norms through Cooperative Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the design of multi-agent systems (MAS) where agents develop social norms autonomously through cooperative learning. The traditional approach to instilling desired social behaviors in MAS often relies on explicit programming, which can be complex, inflexible, and difficult to scale. This research proposes a new methodology centered on leveraging learning mechanisms, specifically cooperative learning, to allow agents to organically establish social norms. The core of the system is a reward function that encourages conformity to emerging norms and penalizes disruptive actions. We explore the dynamics of this system, analyzing how agents converge on shared behaviors without pre-defined rules. The key contribution lies in the shift from explicitly coding social behavior to allowing it to 'emerge' through interaction and learning. We present a theoretical framework for understanding this process, focusing on concepts like norm formation, conformity, and the influence of the reward function. The system's performance is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach. The results suggest that MAS equipped with this learning-based mechanism can effectively establish and maintain social norms, offering a potentially more robust and adaptable solution compared to traditional programming methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Structure Parameter Adjustment for Optimization of Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology structure parameter adjustment (DTSPA) to optimize complex systems. Complex systems often exhibit dynamic behavior, necessitating strategies that can adapt to changing conditions. Traditional optimization methods frequently rely on static approaches, limiting their ability to effectively address these dynamic requirements. This work proposes a novel DTSPA algorithm that dynamically adjusts topology parameters to mimic complex system behavior and enhance performance and response times. The core mechanism involves simulating the dynamic behavior of the system using a dynamic topology framework, followed by optimization of these simulated dynamics. The benefits of this approach include improved stability, responsiveness, and the potential for enhanced performance across various complex system scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through a series of simulations, illustrating its capability to effectively optimize complex systems.

title: Multi-Agent Simulation with Causal Discovery and Intervention Learning
abstract: Multi-agent simulations are increasingly utilized to model complex systems, ranging from social networks to ecological interactions. However, a significant challenge lies in the creation of accurate and dynamic models, frequently relying on extensive manual design and parameter tuning. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates causal discovery algorithms with intervention learning within a multi-agent simulation framework. The system automatically identifies causal relationships among agents, allowing for adaptive simulation behavior and enabling agents to actively manipulate their environment to achieve specific objectives. This method addresses the limitations of traditional simulations by reducing the need for expert-defined models, promoting greater realism, and enhancing the system's adaptability to changing conditions. The core of the system lies in a feedback loop: causal discovery iteratively refines the simulation model, while intervention learning allows agents to strategically modify their environment based on learned causal knowledge. This approach offers a pathway towards more robust and intelligent multi-agent simulations.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Parameter Adjustment via Quantum Topology
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but achieving optimal performance requires careful parameter tuning. Conventional optimization algorithms often require manual adjustments, limiting scalability and efficiency. This paper proposes a novel algorithm, based on quantum topology, for adaptive parameter adjustment in quantum computing. We introduce a mechanism that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to automatically adjust parameters, leading to optimized computational results. The algorithm's core is the utilization of quantum topology to dynamically modify the quantum state, facilitating a pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum computation. We detail the algorithm's design, its theoretical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for improved parameter optimization. This work presents a paradigm shift toward automated parameter tuning, promising significant advancements in quantum algorithm design and performance.

title: Decentralized Verification of Quantum Circuits via Blockchain
abstract: The verification of quantum circuits presents a significant challenge due to the exponential complexity associated with simulating quantum systems. Traditional methods are often computationally intractable for larger circuits. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum circuit verification leveraging blockchain technology. The core idea is to create a decentralized, immutable record of quantum circuit executions. Each execution is represented as a transaction on the blockchain, incorporating circuit parameters, measurement results, and cryptographic hashes. Consensus mechanisms are employed to ensure the integrity and validity of the recorded data, mitigating the risk of manipulation or fraudulent results. This system offers a potential solution to the scalability issues inherent in current verification strategies and contributes to the broader field of quantum security and trust. The system aims to provide a verifiable audit trail for quantum computations, crucial for building confidence in quantum technologies.

title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: A Distributed Approach
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed machine learning, termed Federated Learning with Differential Privacy (FLDP), which addresses the critical challenge of privacy preservation in collaborative model training. Traditional federated learning techniques, while mitigating the risks associated with centralized data collection, still expose model updates, potentially revealing sensitive information about the underlying data. FLDP overcomes this limitation by directly applying differential privacy to the model aggregation process. Specifically, we introduce a locally sensitive differential privacy mechanism that injects noise into each node's model update before aggregation. This ensures that the impact of any single node's contribution on the global model is bounded, effectively protecting individual data privacy. The proposed method allows for reliable model convergence while rigorously upholding privacy guarantees. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of FLDP through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key contribution of this work lies in the shift from applying differential privacy solely to data training to directly incorporating it into the model aggregation phase, creating a more robust and privacy-preserving distributed learning system.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Procedural Content Generation with Aesthetic Constraints
abstract: This paper explores the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to procedural content generation (PCG) with explicit aesthetic constraints. Traditional PCG methods often rely on predefined rules and algorithms, which can lead to repetitive or predictable outcomes. We propose a novel framework utilizing a GAN architecture to address this limitation. The generator network produces content according to specified procedural rules, while the discriminator network learns to distinguish between aesthetically pleasing and displeasing content, effectively incorporating subjective aesthetic preferences into the generation process. We formulate this as a minimax game, where the generator attempts to fool the discriminator, and the discriminator strives to correctly identify aesthetically flawed content. Mathematical formulations detail the loss functions for both networks, emphasizing the adversarial training process. The core claim is that GANs can be trained to generate content that satisfies both procedural rules and subjective aesthetic criteria. This approach offers a pathway to creating more diverse and engaging content, particularly in domains such as game level design, music composition, and digital art. The paper outlines the architecture, training methodology, and potential applications of this GAN-based PCG system.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Non-Linear Adaptive Graph Structures
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adaptive graph structure designed to enhance data representation and facilitate self-adaptive adjustments. Traditional graph algorithms often rely on predefined patterns, limiting adaptability. We introduce a "Dynamic Adaptive Graph Structure Adjustment" mechanism that dynamically adjusts graph parameters based on data noise and error, circumventing local optima and enabling robust self-optimization. The core of this approach lies in learning data representations through an iterative adjustment process, fostering a more resilient and responsive graph structure. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this mechanism through theoretical analysis and simulated experiments, highlighting its potential for improved data representation and adaptive graph design.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Machine Learning Model Optimization explores the potential of leveraging quantum algorithms to dramatically improve the training process of machine learning models, particularly in parameter optimization and hyperparameter selection. This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms, specifically quantum approximate optimization algorithms (QAOA), to accelerate the training of complex models. The core claim is that utilizing quantum computing will yield substantial improvements in model performance and efficiency compared to traditional machine learning techniques. The research will detail the process of applying QAOA to a specific model type and will present results demonstrating the potential for enhanced training speed and improved model accuracy. This work offers a novel approach to optimizing machine learning models using quantum principles.

title: 拓扑虫群论的自适应进化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm based on the principles of topology-crossover, a framework inspired by the self-organization of insect societies. The algorithm aims to identify key biological characteristics – such as co-evolutionary relationships and emergent complexity – by simulating the evolution of biological communities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of evolutionary iterations, revealing patterns and insights that are not readily accessible through traditional evolutionary methods. The core mechanism involves simulating the development of evolutionary dynamics within a network of interconnected organisms, mirroring the structure and behavior of insect colonies. The resulting data provides a quantitative assessment of the interplay of factors influencing biological complexity. The paper explores the potential of this approach for modeling biological evolution, particularly in scenarios involving intricate ecological interactions. This work represents a significant step towards a more holistic understanding of biological systems.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a unique pathway for information encoding. The proposed approach offers a promising avenue for advancing information security through the exploitation of quantum phenomena.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Theory: Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability field theory framework designed for adaptive optimization and machine learning. Traditional optimization algorithms often fall short in dynamic environments, requiring static parameter adjustments. We propose a system where a dynamic probability field adjusts parameters in real-time, enabling complex system optimization and self-adaptive learning. This approach leverages the synergistic combination of probability field dynamics and adaptive learning, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a continuously adjusting probability field that responds to system state, facilitating rapid parameter adjustments and improved performance. We detail the framework's design, its advantages, and potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology to neural network architectures, focusing on dynamically adjusting the network's connectivity and layer configurations based on input data characteristics. Traditional neural networks often rely on fixed topologies, limiting their ability to effectively learn complex patterns. This research proposes a reinforcement learning-inspired mechanism to intelligently adjust network structure, enhancing robustness and generalization capabilities. The core claim centers on creating a system that adapts to the data, resulting in more resilient and versatile AI models. We explore a novel framework incorporating feedback loops and a learned reward function to guide topology optimization. This paper presents a detailed design and implementation of this adaptive topology system, demonstrating its efficacy through simulations and preliminary experiments. The results highlight the significant advantages of dynamic topology compared to static architectures in handling diverse input data.

title: The Three Dividends: Governance, Protocol, and Architecture Economics in Protocol- Governed Systems
abstract: This paper analyzes the lifecycle, complexity, and implementation economics of protocol-governed architecture. Building on the structural taxonomy (Paper 3) [Bachi, 2026c], governance mechanics (Paper 4) [Bachi, 2026d], deterministic enforcement (Paper 6) [Bachi, 2026f], and mutation bounding (Paper 7) [Bachi, 2026g], we model how constitutional separation affects long-term system evolution, incremental domain implementation cost, and human cognitive scaling. We define three complementary economic properties. The Governance Dividend is the reduction in structural entropy, maintenance volatility, and behavioral drift achieved through explicit behavioral law and bounded mutation surfaces — operating at the organizational and lifecycle level. The Protocol Dividend is the reduction in marginal domain implementation cost achieved by separating governance from execution — operating at the implementation level. The Architecture Dividend is the structural reduction of human cognitive load achieved by relocating behavioral complexity from application code into governed protocol artifacts — operating at the human and team level. Together, they constitute the complete economic case for protocol governance.

title: How Do You Hear a Quantum Computer Whisper?
abstract: Quantum transduction is the process of upconverting microwave quantum signals into optical signals to develop quantum networks through optical fibers outside the dilution refrigerator, enabling connections between quantum technologies on the quantum internet. In this project, upconversion is achieved by directing an optical laser and the microwave quantum signal into an electro-optic bulk crystal. The crystal is housed within a Superconducting Radio Frequency (SRF) cavity designed to maximize the overlap between the microwave field and the crystal volume. In the presence of microwaves, the refractive index of the crystal changes through the Pockels effect. This change in refractive index modifies the propagation of the optical field within the crystal, allowing the quantum information carried by the microwave field to be transferred to the optical field. This study focuses on coupling laser light from suspended waveguide chips into the whispering-gallery modes (WGMs) of the crystal to enable transduction. The coupling efficiency between the optical field in the suspended waveguide and the WGM depends on the position of the laser spot on the crystal. To address this challenge, a feedback-based algorithm is being developed to fine-tune the waveguide position so that the optical signal is coupled efficiently into the crystal. After passing through the crystal, the optical signal is detected by a photodiode connected to an oscilloscope. The algorithm evaluates the coupling quality and iteratively adjusts the waveguide position to maximize coupling efficiency. The expected outcome is an automated waveguide alignment method that improves optical coupling and enables more efficient microwave-to-optical quantum transduction.

title: Beyond Rational Concession: Designing an Emotion-Driven "Monster Parent" Agent for Teacher Training
abstract: Monster parents, guardians who make unreasonable demands on teachers, are a growing source of occupational stress in schools. Simulation-based training offers a safe and reproducible alternative to costly in-person role-playing exercises. This paper first presents the conceptual design of a virtual monster-parent agent for teacher training, arguing that interactions with monster parents constitute a form of irrational, emotion-driven negotiation that is fundamentally different from the rational, bilateral negotiations addressed in prior work. It then describes the current implementation of the training platform, including the classroom environment, avatar character, voice, and facial expressions. Finally, we report the results of a pilot study investigating the effects of the agent’s emotional expressions. The findings provide encouraging evidence supporting the feasibility of the proposed approach and motivate the further development of the system.

title: Concept of a Sensor Test Environment for Dusty Agricultural Conditions
abstract: Dust in agriculture presents a significant challenge for autonomous agricultural machinery. Dust can impair the performance of sensors and algorithms. This work, therefore, presents a concept for a proving ground consisting of an indoor and outdoor area. The indoor area comprises a laboratory test bench where dust circulates in a closed system and a test hall where life-size objects can be placed. The outdoor area features dedicated test setups that enable reproducible data to be recorded with and without dust during real-world agriculture work. The proving ground and the setups are visualized in 3D.

title: Test-time adaptation for speech enhancement with an autoregressive speech prior
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) offers a promising direction for improving speech enhancement models under mismatched acoustic conditions, without requiring access to labeled target data. In this work, we propose a single-utterance TTA method that regularizes a pretrained speech enhancement model using an autoregressive prior trained on clean speech latent representations extracted from a neural audio codec. Adaptation is performed by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the enhanced speech distribution and the clean speech prior. Experiments across multiple noisy speech datasets show consistent improvements in speech quality, particularly under training-testing noise mismatch conditions. Code and audio examples are available online.

title: SurgeGen: A Hybrid Generative Diffusion Framework for Storm Surge Scenario Synthesis
abstract: Predicting storm surge induced by landfalling tropical cyclones is crucial for flood mitigation and coastal risk management. Traditionally, physics-based numerical models simulate storm surge by solving the Navier--Stokes equations using numerical methods, but these simulations are computationally expensive. Generative models are promising for storm surge emulation because they can generate diverse realizations rather than producing a single deterministic prediction. However, their use for storm surge emulation remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we leverage diffusion models for storm surge surrogate modeling, combining a baseline prediction stage with conditional generation to provide a more interpretable modeling framework. We develop SurgeGen, a two-stage generative framework for generating storm surge scenarios conditioned on hypothetical storms with parameters defined in a continuous space. First, a baseline model produces a coarse estimate of the storm surge height. This estimate then conditions a diffusion model, which generates refined storm surge scenarios that better capture spatial patterns and variability. We demonstrate that our approach can generate realistic and diverse storm surge scenarios under conditions both within and outside the training distribution.

title: Validation expérimentale d’une méthode d’apprentissage de similarité sur des données de patients en oncologie
abstract: Patient prognosis prediction based on clinical and laboratory data represents a major challenge in medicine. In this context, Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) enables prediction by relying on similarity between a new patient and previously observed cases. This work focuses on the CoAT method and investigates whether the CCoSiL metric learning framework, which aims to learn a similarity measure tailored to the prediction task, genuinely enhances its predictive performance. The study investigates overall survival prediction for pancreatic cancer patients, formulated as a three-class classification task (early death, intermediate survival, long-term survival). It is conducted on a real-world cohort extracted from the AP-HP Clinical Data Warehouse (EDS), combining clinical, biological, and tumoral features. The performance of CoAT coupled with CCoSiL is compared against an alternative metric learning method (LMNN), as well as baseline approaches including k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) and logistic regression. Experimental results demonstrate first that metric optimization via CCoSiL systematically improves the performance of analogical models compared to an unlearned metric. Compared to reference methods, CCoSiL outperforms both the generic LMNN metric and the baseline k-NN classifier. Finally, one of the CCoAT variants achieves F1 scores comparable to, and at times higher than, logistic regression, while preserving case-level explainability through patient comparison.

title: DATA MINING PARA ANÁLISIS DE TEXTO LIBRE RECIBIDO EN LLAMADAS DE EMERGENCIAS POR EL CENTRO REGULADOR SAMU ARAUCANÍA SUR.
abstract: El Servicio de Atención Médica de Urgencias (SAMU) enfrenta dificultades para identificar de manera eficiente casos críticos como politraumatismos y paros cardiorrespiratorios, ya que sus registros se realizan en texto libre en hojas de cálculo, lo que obliga a un análisis manual propenso a errores. Para abordar este problema, se desarrolló una herramienta basada en técnicas de minería de datos y procesamiento de lenguaje natural (PLN), que permite automatizar la detección de estos eventos a partir de los registros clínicos del año 2024. El proyecto consideró cinco fases: levantamiento de datos en terreno, preprocesamiento textual, desarrollo del modelo de clasificación, pruebas piloto con usuarios y entrega final. Se emplearon algoritmos de aprendizaje supervisado y representaciones vectoriales de texto para construir un modelo capaz de identificar patrones asociados a eventos críticos. Esta solución mejora la precisión en la clasificación de casos, reduce significativamente la carga manual y permite emitir reportes más consistentes y oportunos al Ministerio de Salud. Su implementación aporta una herramienta escalable y reutilizable que puede integrarse a otros sistemas de atención prehospitalaria, fortaleciendo la capacidad de respuesta ante emergencias y apoyando la toma de decisiones en salud pública.

title: Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement: A Non-Linear Geometric Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the multifaceted behavior of multi-body quantum entanglement within the context of non-linear geometric spaces. We propose a novel quantum geometric model that aims to simulate and understand the unique characteristics of quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves linking quantum entanglement to non-linear geometry, allowing for a more intuitive representation of complex entanglement dynamics. This work contributes to a foundation for advanced computational methods reliant on a quantum geometric framework. The resulting model offers a fundamentally different approach to analyzing and manipulating entangled states, potentially unlocking new avenues for quantum information processing and security.

title: High-Dimensional Matrix Tensor Representation and Automatic Graph Construction
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for constructing complex graphs from high-dimensional matrix representations, leveraging a unique approach based on matrix feature representation and neighbor relationship analysis. The core mechanism centers around a "tensorization" technique that automatically generates the graph, enabling efficient data analysis and modeling through the structural insights of the graph. We propose a new algorithm that minimizes redundant connections and prioritizes the establishment of robust, interconnected graphs. This approach offers a significant improvement over traditional methods by automating the graph construction process and enhancing the model's ability to capture intricate relationships within the data. The resulting graph structure is designed to facilitate deeper insights into the underlying data distribution. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through illustrative examples and a comparative analysis with established graph construction techniques.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on a dynamically adjusted "on-the-fly" matrix derived from a logarithmic function. The algorithm aims to address the limitations of traditional optimization methods, particularly when dealing with complex data distributions and varying gradient characteristics. The core innovation lies in the design of a mechanism that adjusts the logarithmic matrix during the optimization process, enabling adaptive parameter tuning and improved efficiency. We present a rigorous analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of optimization problems. The paper concludes with a detailed explanation of the underlying mathematical principles and highlights the potential implications for various scientific and engineering applications.

title: Dynamic Topology Matrices for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: The development of adaptive machine learning models has become increasingly important in recent years, particularly in the face of complex and non-linear data. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on predefined parameters, which can limit the model's ability to effectively handle data intricacies. This paper explores the application of dynamic topology matrices to address this challenge. We introduce a novel matrix representation that dynamically adjusts its structure and weights during training based on the data's inherent properties. This adaptive approach aims to enhance model performance, specifically in scenarios where data exhibits complex nonlinear relationships. We present a framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in optimizing machine learning models for tasks involving non-linear data. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic topology construction and adjustment process, enabling the matrix to self-optimize and adapt to the data's characteristics. This research contributes to a new paradigm in machine learning, moving beyond static parameter tuning to a more intelligent and adaptive approach.

Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on predefined parameters, which can limit the model's ability to effectively handle data intricacies. This paper explores the application of dynamic topology matrices to address this challenge. We introduce a novel matrix representation that dynamically adjusts its structure and weights during training based on the data's inherent properties. This adaptive approach aims to enhance model performance, specifically in scenarios where data exhibits complex nonlinear relationships. We present a framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in optimizing machine learning models for tasks involving non-linear data. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic topology construction and adjustment process, enabling the matrix to self-optimize and adapt to the data's characteristics. This research contributes to a new paradigm in machine learning, moving beyond static parameter tuning to a more intelligent and adaptive approach.

title: 基于拓扑结构的自适应语言模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel language model architecture, termed "Adaptive Topological Language Model" (ATLM), that leverages the inherent topological structure of language to enhance prediction accuracy and expressive power. Traditional language models often rely on statistical associations between words, neglecting the underlying relationships that govern language. The ATPM dynamically adjusts its parameters through an adaptive learning process, effectively capturing and utilizing the structural information embedded within text. The core mechanism involves representing the language as a graph and employing a self-organizing map (SOM) to identify and refine the topological features crucial for language modeling. This approach significantly improves the model's ability to capture semantic relationships and generate coherent text. We demonstrate the superior performance of the ATPM through extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential to advance language modeling research.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Linear Geometric Quantities Generation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity to generate complex mathematical structures. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum entanglement mechanism to produce geometric quantities with non-linear properties, offering a potential pathway for advancing quantum information and quantum computing research. We propose a method leveraging the non-linearity inherent in entanglement to transform quantum states into a tailored geometric representation, which will then be employed to optimize quantum computation. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant departure from traditional quantum computing implementations, potentially unlocking new avenues for understanding and controlling quantum systems.
